# plugin.yaml reference: manifest format 1

<!-- Generated by `wf integration schema --markdown`. Do not edit by hand:
     change workflow_engine/schemas/plugin-manifest-1.json and regenerate. -->

This is the contract for an extension's `plugin.yaml`. `wf integration schema`
prints it as JSON Schema. `wf integration lint <dir>` checks a manifest against
it; add `--json` for a result a script can read. Lint also requires at least
one `integrations:` entry, so a plugin without pollers fails on that one rule;
its field findings (the errors that say "not a manifest field") still apply.

## The format number

- Put `manifest: 1` first. A manifest without it is read as format 1, and
  lint warns until you add it.
- An engine refuses a format newer than it reads. When the manifest sets an
  `engine:` floor, the message names that version to update to. Engines released before the `manifest:` key
  existed ignore it, so a manifest in a newer format should also set an
  `engine:` floor.
- New optional fields can arrive in any release without a new format number.
  An older engine ignores a field it does not know, so set `engine:` to the
  release you built and tested against.

## Stability

- **stable**: within format 1 the field keeps its name, type and meaning.
  It changes only through the deprecation rule below, or in a new format.
- **experimental**: the field may change or go in any release.

## Deprecation

A stable field is renamed or removed in three steps:

1. The replacement ships, and the old field is marked deprecated with the
   release that deprecated it, its replacement and a removal date.
2. The old field keeps loading for **at least 90 days**. Lint and install warn
   and name the replacement.
3. It stops loading only after that date, in a release whose notes say so.

## Unknown fields

- `wf integration lint` reports any field not listed below as an error, with a
  "did you mean" when a listed field is close.
- `wf plugin install` prints the same report as warnings, then installs.
- At load, these blocks refuse a field they do not list, so the manifest does
  not install: `settings[]`, `settings[].rows[]`, `integrations[].presentation`, `integrations[].settings`, `integrations[].settings.rows[]`, `integrations[].intake`, `actions[]`, `actions[].args.*`, `onboarding_probes[]`, `requires`, `installs.*`, `installs.*.system`, `installs.*.system.apt`, `installs.*.system.apt.source`, `installs.*.system.dnf`, `installs.*.system.brew`, `installs.*.user`, `permissions`. Everywhere else the engine ignores an unknown field.

## Fields

`[]` means each item of a list, and `*` means any key of a mapping.
"Required" means required within its block: `config[].key` is needed in each
`config` item, not in every manifest.

| Field | Type | Required | Stability | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest` | integer |  | stable | The manifest format MAJOR, a whole number. Absent means 1. |
| `name` | string | yes | stable | The extension's name. Its actions are invoked as `<name>.<action>`. |
| `version` | string | yes | stable | The extension's version, plain numeric `x.y.z`. |
| `description` | string |  | stable | One paragraph on what the extension does. |
| `author` | string |  | stable | Who wrote it. |
| `homepage` | string |  | stable | Where to read more. |
| `license` | string |  | stable | The license name, such as MIT. |
| `tags` | list of string |  | stable | Free-form labels. |
| `depends` | mapping of name to string |  | stable | Other extensions this one needs: extension name to version spec (`>=X.Y.Z`, `^X.Y.Z`, `==X.Y.Z` or a bare `X.Y.Z`). |
| `engine` | string |  | stable | The lowest engine this extension runs on, as a version spec such as `>=1.2.42`. Install refuses an engine below it. |
| `config` | list of mapping |  | stable | The extension's own env keys, the ones its hooks and bin/ scripts read. |
| `config[].key` | string | yes | stable | The env var name. |
| `config[].type` | one of `bool`, `csv`, `enum`, `int`, `secret`, `string` | yes | stable | The field type the dashboard form renders. |
| `config[].label` | string |  | stable | The form label. |
| `config[].description` | string |  | stable | Help text under the field. |
| `config[].default` | any |  | stable | The value used when none is set, stored as a string. |
| `config[].required` | boolean |  | stable | Whether a value must be set. Defaults to true when there is no `default`. |
| `config[].options_from` | one of `checkpoint_states`, `workflow_names` |  | stable | Where an `enum` field's options come from. |
| `config[].danger` | boolean |  | stable | Marks a field whose change needs care. |
| `settings` | list of mapping |  | stable | Settings-page groups for the plugin's own top-level `config:` keys. A single `{group, rows}` mapping is also accepted. |
| `settings[].group` | string | yes | stable | The Settings page group title. |
| `settings[].rows` | list of mapping | yes | stable | One row per config key shown. |
| `settings[].rows[].key` | string | yes | stable | A non-secret key of this integration's own `config`. |
| `settings[].rows[].control` | one of `multi`, `select`, `stepper`, `text`, `toggle` |  | stable | The control. It must fit the key's type, and defaults from it. |
| `settings[].rows[].label` | string |  | stable | The row label. |
| `settings[].rows[].help` | string |  | stable | Help text. |
| `settings[].rows[].applies` | string |  | stable | The rest of the sentence "applies ...". |
| `settings[].rows[].options_from` | one of `checkpoint_states`, `workflow_names` |  | stable | Where a multi or select row's options come from. |
| `settings[].rows[].show_if` | string |  | stable | Another toggle row of this block that must be on for this row to show. |
| `settings[].rows[].confirm` | string |  | stable | A question asked before a change is saved. |
| `connections` | list of mapping |  | stable | Shared credential groups that integrations name in `uses` and actions name in `connection`. |
| `connections[].name` | string | yes | stable | The connection's name, unique in this manifest. |
| `connections[].label` | string |  | stable | The name the dashboard shows. |
| `connections[].fields` | list of mapping | yes | stable | The credentials this connection holds. |
| `connections[].fields[].key` | string | yes | stable | The env var name. |
| `connections[].fields[].type` | one of `bool`, `csv`, `enum`, `int`, `secret`, `string` | yes | stable | The field type. |
| `connections[].fields[].label` | string |  | stable | The form label. |
| `connections[].fields[].description` | string |  | stable | Help text under the field. |
| `connections[].fields[].default` | any |  | stable | The value used when none is set, stored as a string. |
| `connections[].fields[].required` | boolean |  | stable | Whether a value must be set. Defaults to true when there is no `default`. |
| `connections[].verify` | string |  | stable | A command that checks the credentials work, run from the workspace. |
| `integrations` | list of mapping |  | stable | Pollers `wf loop` runs on a schedule. |
| `integrations[].name` | string | yes | stable | The poller's name, unique on the board. |
| `integrations[].run` | string | yes | stable | The script to run, relative to the extension (`hooks/poll.py`). |
| `integrations[].label` | string |  | stable | The name the dashboard shows. |
| `integrations[].description` | string |  | stable | What the poller does. |
| `integrations[].timeout_seconds` | integer |  | stable | How long one run may take. Absent or 0 means the engine's default (120 s); the ceiling is 1800 s. |
| `integrations[].interval_seconds` | integer |  | stable | The least time between runs. 0 means every pass of the loop's integrations thread (every 300 s unless WF_INTEGRATION_INTERVAL says otherwise). |
| `integrations[].enabled` | boolean |  | stable | Whether it runs after install. Defaults to true. |
| `integrations[].uses` | list of string |  | stable | The `connections` this poller reads. |
| `integrations[].config` | list of mapping |  | stable | This poller's own env keys. |
| `integrations[].config[].key` | string | yes | stable | The env var name. |
| `integrations[].config[].type` | one of `bool`, `csv`, `enum`, `int`, `secret`, `string` | yes | stable | The field type the dashboard form renders. |
| `integrations[].config[].label` | string |  | stable | The form label. |
| `integrations[].config[].description` | string |  | stable | Help text under the field. |
| `integrations[].config[].default` | any |  | stable | The value used when none is set, stored as a string. |
| `integrations[].config[].required` | boolean |  | stable | Whether a value must be set. Defaults to true when there is no `default`. |
| `integrations[].config[].options_from` | one of `checkpoint_states`, `workflow_names` |  | stable | Where an `enum` field's options come from. |
| `integrations[].config[].danger` | boolean |  | stable | Marks a field whose change needs care. |
| `integrations[].presentation` | mapping |  | stable | How the Extensions page names and files this poller's card. |
| `integrations[].presentation.name` | string |  | stable | The card's title. |
| `integrations[].presentation.group` | one of `engine`, `incoming`, `questions`, `shipping`, `pr_followups`, `housekeeping`, `updates` |  | stable | The Extensions page group the card is filed under. |
| `integrations[].presentation.what` | string |  | stable | One line on what the poller does. |
| `integrations[].presentation.activity` | string |  | stable | A sentence with `{field}` placeholders filled from the poller's status card. |
| `integrations[].settings` | mapping |  | stable | Rows this poller adds to the Settings page. |
| `integrations[].settings.group` | string | yes | stable | The Settings page group title. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows` | list of mapping | yes | stable | One row per config key shown. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].key` | string | yes | stable | A non-secret key of this integration's own `config`. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].control` | one of `multi`, `select`, `stepper`, `text`, `toggle` |  | stable | The control. It must fit the key's type, and defaults from it. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].label` | string |  | stable | The row label. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].help` | string |  | stable | Help text. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].applies` | string |  | stable | The rest of the sentence "applies ...". |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].options_from` | one of `checkpoint_states`, `workflow_names` |  | stable | Where a multi or select row's options come from. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].show_if` | string |  | stable | Another toggle row of this block that must be on for this row to show. |
| `integrations[].settings.rows[].confirm` | string |  | stable | A question asked before a change is saved. |
| `integrations[].dry_run` | boolean |  | stable | The poller skips its external writes when `WF_DRY_RUN=1`. Without it `wf integration run --dry-run` refuses the poller. Defaults to false. |
| `integrations[].intake` | mapping |  | stable | Whether the items this poller seeds may start Triage without a click when the board lists the provider in `WF_INTAKE_AUTO_APPROVE`. Absent means untrusted. |
| `integrations[].intake.provider` | string | yes | stable | The provider name the poller writes on each item it seeds (`context.intake.source.provider`). It must be the integration's own `name`: an integration vouches only for its own items. |
| `integrations[].intake.trust` | one of `trusted`, `per-item`, `untrusted` | yes | stable | `trusted`: the poller only seeds items a person already chose to send. `per-item`: each item says so itself, and only one whose `context.intake.attributes.extra.triage_trust.trusted` is `true` may start Triage without a click. `untrusted`: none may. |
| `hooks` | list of mapping |  | stable | Every script in hooks/, with where it belongs. |
| `hooks[].run` | string | yes | stable | The script, relative to the extension (`hooks/check.py`). |
| `hooks[].kind` | one of `command`, `library`, `poller`, `workflow-hook` | yes | stable | Where the script belongs. |
| `hooks[].attach` | list of one of `on_checkpoint`, `on_init`, `on_state_change`, `on_terminal`, `on_unblock`, `post`, `pre`, `requires` |  | stable | Where a `workflow-hook` attaches. Required for that kind, refused for the others. |
| `hooks[].description` | string |  | stable | What the script does. |
| `actions` | list of mapping |  | stable | What an agent may do through one of this extension's connections, invoked as `<name>.<action>`. |
| `actions[].name` | string | yes | stable | The action's name, with no dot. |
| `actions[].connection` | string | yes | stable | One of this manifest's `connections`. |
| `actions[].label` | string | yes | stable | A short title. |
| `actions[].when` | string | yes | stable | When an agent should use it. |
| `actions[].args` | mapping of name to mapping |  | stable | Arg name to its declaration. |
| `actions[].args.*.type` | one of `bool`, `csv`, `int`, `path`, `string` | yes | stable | The arg type. |
| `actions[].args.*.required` | boolean |  | stable | Whether the caller must pass it. |
| `actions[].args.*.max_bytes` | integer |  | stable | The largest file a `path` arg accepts. |
| `actions[].command` | string | yes | stable | The command to run, from the workspace. Args arrive as JSON on stdin. |
| `actions[].switch` | string |  | stable | An env var that turns the action off when false. |
| `actions[].effect` | one of `read`, `write` | yes | stable | Whether it changes anything. A `write` needs a grant in the step's `uses`. |
| `actions[].timeout_seconds` | integer |  | stable | How long one run may take, a positive whole number. |
| `actions[].dry_run` | boolean |  | stable | The action skips its external writes when `WF_DRY_RUN=1`. Without it `wf act --dry-run` refuses a `write`; a `read` needs none. Defaults to false. |
| `onboarding_probes` | list of mapping |  | stable | Checks `wf doctor --onboarding` runs from the board's repo and grades like a hook: exit 0 proves the claim, 2 is not measurable here, a timeout warns, anything else refuses. Each claim joins the onboarding sign-off and is stated only when its row is ok. |
| `onboarding_probes[].name` | string | yes | stable | The probe's name, unique in this manifest. Its doctor row is `<plugin>.<name>`. |
| `onboarding_probes[].claim` | string | yes | stable | What a passing probe proves, as a clause of the sign-off sentence: one line starting with `to `, at most 120 characters. |
| `onboarding_probes[].command` | string | yes | stable | The command to run, from the board's repo, with the env a poller gets plus `WF_REPO_DIR` and `WF_WORKSPACE_DIR`. |
| `onboarding_probes[].timeout_seconds` | integer |  | stable | How long one run may take, 1 to 3600. Defaults to 120. A probe that overruns is a warning and is not retried. |
| `onboarding_probes[].opt_in` | boolean |  | stable | The probe spends real runs, so doctor runs it only with `--smoke`; without it the probe's claim is not proven. Defaults to false. |
| `requires` | mapping |  | stable | What must already be installed before this extension installs. |
| `requires.workflows` | list of string |  | stable | Workflow names that must already be installed. |
| `installs` | mapping of name to mapping |  | stable | How to install each item a lane declares (a tool, a CLI plugin, an MCP server, a skill), by item name: one recipe per name. A machine takes the first `system` route whose package manager it has (apt, then dnf, then brew), else the `user` steps, else the item is named with the recipe's `fix`. Two installed extensions with different recipes for one name: it is not installed. A malformed recipe refuses the manifest at load. |
| `installs.*.needs` | list of string |  | stable | Items installed before this one, by name. |
| `installs.*.system` | mapping |  | stable | Package-manager routes: admin on Linux, as the user with brew. The engine writes each command; a recipe names packages only. |
| `installs.*.system.apt` | mapping |  | stable | Debian, Ubuntu: `sudo apt-get install -y <packages>`. |
| `installs.*.system.apt.packages` | list of string | yes | stable | The package names: lowercase letters, digits and `+._-`, starting with a letter or digit, and not ending in `-` (apt removes a package so named) or `.rpm`/`.deb` (a file, to dnf). |
| `installs.*.system.apt.source` | mapping |  | stable | An apt repository the engine adds first: it writes the key and the list line into files itself. |
| `installs.*.system.apt.source.key` | string | yes | stable | The repository's signing key, an https:// URL. |
| `installs.*.system.apt.source.list` | string | yes | stable | One sources.list line: `deb [options] https://<host>/<path> <suite> [<component> ...]`. |
| `installs.*.system.apt.run` | list of list of string |  | stable | Steps run as the user after the packages: a list of argv lists, never a shell. |
| `installs.*.system.dnf` | mapping |  | stable | Fedora, RHEL: `sudo dnf install -y <packages>`. |
| `installs.*.system.dnf.packages` | list of string | yes | stable | The package names: lowercase letters, digits and `+._-`, starting with a letter or digit, and not ending in `-` (apt removes a package so named) or `.rpm`/`.deb` (a file, to dnf). |
| `installs.*.system.dnf.run` | list of list of string |  | stable | Steps run as the user after the packages: a list of argv lists, never a shell. |
| `installs.*.system.brew` | mapping |  | stable | Homebrew, as the user: `brew install <packages>`. |
| `installs.*.system.brew.packages` | list of string | yes | stable | The package names: lowercase letters, digits and `+._-`, starting with a letter or digit, and not ending in `-` (apt removes a package so named) or `.rpm`/`.deb` (a file, to dnf). |
| `installs.*.system.brew.run` | list of list of string |  | stable | Steps run as the user after the packages: a list of argv lists, never a shell. |
| `installs.*.user` | mapping |  | stable | Steps run as the user, never under sudo, on a machine no `system` route fits. |
| `installs.*.user.script` | string |  | stable | The vendor's installer, an https:// URL the engine downloads and runs with sh. Set this or `run`, not both. |
| `installs.*.user.run` | list of list of string |  | stable | A list of argv lists, such as `[[tool, plugin, install, name]]`, never a shell. Set this or `script`, not both. |
| `installs.*.none` | boolean |  | stable | The engine cannot install this item. Needs a `fix`, and takes no `system`, `user` or `needs`. Defaults to false. |
| `installs.*.fix` | string |  | stable | One line a person acts on when no route fits this machine, or when `none` is true. |
| `listing` | mapping |  | stable | The store listing: display text the engine never acts on. A bad listing still installs; lint fails on it and `wf plugin info` shows why. |
| `listing.title` | string |  | stable | The store title. Absent means the first integration's `presentation.name`, else `name`. |
| `listing.summary` | string |  | stable | One line on what the extension does, at most 120 characters. |
| `listing.publisher` | mapping |  | stable | Who publishes the extension. |
| `listing.publisher.id` | string | yes | stable | A lowercase id such as `example-co`. |
| `listing.publisher.name` | string | yes | stable | The name shown. |
| `listing.publisher.url` | string |  | stable | The publisher's http(s) address. |
| `listing.categories` | list of one of `engine`, `incoming`, `questions`, `shipping`, `pr_followups`, `housekeeping`, `updates` |  | stable | The Extensions page groups the listing is filed under. |
| `listing.icon` | string |  | stable | A PNG, JPEG or WebP file inside the extension folder, at most 1 MiB. No SVG. |
| `listing.screenshots` | list of mapping |  | stable | At most 5 screenshots. |
| `listing.screenshots[].path` | string | yes | stable | A PNG, JPEG or WebP file inside the extension folder, at most 1 MiB. No SVG. |
| `listing.screenshots[].caption` | string |  | stable | A line under the screenshot. |
| `listing.readme` | string |  | stable | A file inside the extension folder shown as the long description. |
| `listing.changelog` | string |  | stable | A file inside the extension folder listing what changed per version. |
| `listing.links` | mapping |  | stable | Links shown on the listing. |
| `listing.links.docs` | string |  | stable | The documentation's http(s) address. |
| `listing.links.source` | string |  | stable | The source code's http(s) address. |
| `listing.links.issues` | string |  | stable | Where to report a problem, an http(s) address. |
| `listing.links.privacy` | string |  | stable | The privacy policy's http(s) address. |
| `listing.support` | mapping |  | stable | Where users get help. |
| `listing.support.url` | string |  | stable | The support page's http(s) address. |
| `listing.support.email` | string |  | stable | The support email address. |
| `listing.data_out` | string |  | stable | What data leaves the board and where it goes, in plain words. |
| `permissions` | mapping |  | stable | What the extension reaches that the engine cannot derive from its folder, shown on the consent screen as declared. |
| `permissions.network` | list of string |  | stable | Hosts or URLs the extension calls, or one `{CONFIG_KEY}` naming the config key that holds the host. |
| `permissions.board` | list of string |  | stable | What the extension does to the board beyond its actions, such as `create_tasks` or `context.autonomous`. |
